conviction_note: Q3 volumes, rates and the EBITDA guide (in line with Q2's USD 122m) are already public, so the move turns on two lines that are not out: the Q3 dividend (cut to USD 16m last quarter, -11.9% that day) and the Q4 guide, where VLSFO up 11.7% q-o-q against a 5-6 month BAF lag points to a soft guide. The dividend could go either way, so the sum of the findings is -1.0 and the scaled number is -0.52 on a 6.5% absolute move at p_up 46. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because the dividend line, which is unsourced against any consensus, could swamp the fuel read in either direction.

findings.finding: The pre-released Q3 operating data point to EBITDA at or slightly above the 'in line with Q2' guide: gross rate +5.0% q-o-q (98.8 vs 94.1 USD/cbm) on gradually higher BAF, net rate +2.7% (81.1 vs 79.0), volume flat at 4.0m cbm. Against that, Singapore VLSFO averaged about 5% more than in Q2 (814.5 vs 775.5 USD/mt).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat Bloomberg EBITDA 122 vs 120 and the stock still fell 11.86% on the dividend; Q3 2025 revenue and EBITDA were near consensus and the stock fell 6.73% on the dividend. The EBITDA line has not moved this stock on its own
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The monthly trading updates publish volumes and rates, and the company guided EBITDA. All that is left is a few million dollars of BAF catch-up against the fuel rise, which sits inside the guide.
findings.independence: Peer Wallenius Wilhelmsen's Q3 shipping EBITDA rose 'largely because of a $47 million reduction in net fuel costs' as surcharges caught up (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/dry-cargo/pcc-pctc/wallenius-wilhelmsen-earnings-rise-2026, 2026-11-04). The Q2 quarterly rates are from the Q2 report, https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/attachment?messageId=680262&attachmentId=331494

findings.finding: By the company's own formula, the Q3 dividend is cash above a target minimum balance (about USD 200m, implied by end-Q2 cash of 216m and a 16m payout). Q2's cut came from a one-off working-capital build (receivables -34.3m, bunker inventory -22.7m; operating cash flow 67m against EBITDA 122m) that the company said would normalise in Q3. Debt and lease service ran about 36m a quarter and the remaining equity instalments on the original four newbuilds are only 15m, so a rebound to roughly USD 60-100m is mechanically plausible. Fuel prices still rising keep bunker inventory value high, which caps the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line the stock trades on. Q3 2025: the dividend was '80 prosent under analytikernes forventninger' (80% below what analysts expected) and the stock fell 6.73%. Q2 2026: the dividend was cut to 16m from 94m and the stock fell 11.86%, although EBITDA beat. Q2 2025 paid 137m and the stock rose 5.96%
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The company told the market that cash conversion would normalise, and the stock rose from the NOK 167 placement price to 182. What is not public is the size: no Q3 dividend consensus could be found, and after Q2 Fearnley expected a positive dividend surprise while Nordea expected a disappointment ('Fearnley-analytiker øyner positiv utbytteoverraskelse ..., mens Nordea-analytiker venter skuffelse', i.e. Fearnley's analyst saw a positive dividend surprise coming while Nordea's expected a disappointment). The sign against the bar is genuinely open, so the size is small with a wide range.
findings.independence: The policy wording 'distribute available cash generation above a targeted minimum cash balance, assessed at the end of each quarter' is in the placement release (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680760). The Q2 dividend-shock reaction and analyst disagreement are in https://e24.no/boers-og-finans/i/K8axMe/store-sprik-foer-shipping-fasit (2026-08-19). All of this shares the company's own documents

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is likely to be soft on fuel. Singapore VLSFO has averaged 909.5 USD/mt in Q4 to date against 814.5 in Q3 (+11.7%) and 775.5 in Q2. The company recovers fuel through a surcharge with a '5-6 months time-lag', and it quantified a ~USD 20m short-term timing hit for Q2 when VLSFO rose about 150 USD/mt. The October update adds that 'disruptions to our Middle East service continue to impact network efficiency'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 guided Q4 'slightly below' Q3 plus a ~USD 20m USTR port-fee hit, and the stock fell 6.73% (together with the dividend change). Q4 2025 guided Q1 'slightly above' and the stock rose 3.8%. Q1 2026 flagged a ~USD 20m fuel timing hit plus 10m from the Middle East for Q2, yet the stock rose 4.6% on the 94m dividend
findings.why_not_priced: Bunker prices are public and analysts model the lag, so this is partly priced. But the company's August outlook, written when fuel was about 755-820, promised 'normalized performance with full run-rate BAF compensation' in Q3, and that framing is what the 60-day run-up of +7.7% sits on. Fuel has risen about 12% since, so a guide that re-flags a timing hit would contradict the normalisation story. If it were fully priced, the stock would not have recovered to 182 from 169.6 on 6 November.
findings.independence: The lag mechanism and the 20m quantification are the company's own (Q1 release https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=672827; Q2 release https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680262). The Middle East comment is in the October trading update (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=686156). The fuel series is a single source: a proxy, so this is macro-to-company transmission

findings.finding: The closest peer, Wallenius Wilhelmsen, fell about 2.3% on its Q3 day (4 Nov: NOK 168.0 to 164.1) despite adjusted EBITDA up 19% q-o-q to USD 428m. It kept its FY guide at about USD 1.6bn, below its December range of 1.65-1.75bn, so the sector's operational beats are currently being sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is a peer reaction, not a HAUTO line. HAUTO itself fell 11.86% on a Q2 2026 EBITDA beat
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction-function datum rather than information about HAUTO's numbers. It says the bar for a positive reaction in car carriers is the outlook and the payout, not the quarter. It is weak and indirect.

findings.finding: Peer read on contract renewals: Wallenius Wilhelmsen said its shipping capacity is fully committed for 2026, that most 2027-29 capacity is expected to be contracted by year-end at current market rates, and announced USD 1.7bn of new awards after the quarter. That supports HAUTO commentary on renewals at higher rates, in a market where Höegh says charter prices rose 60% from Q1 to July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HAUTO's 2026-07-10 contract extension (USD 300m) came the same day as the June trading update, and the stock rose 4.47%
findings.why_not_priced: Peer statements are public and HAUTO has said nothing new on renewals since July. Any company-level renewal number would be news, but whether it appears in the release is a guess, so this is small.
findings.independence: HAUTO's own Q2 outlook: 'The capacity market is further tightening with +60% increase in July charter index price vs Q1' (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680262)

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the reported-quarter finding moved from +0.4 to +0.2, because the monthly trading updates pre-release volumes and rates and the EBITDA sits inside the guide

'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': the dividend finding moved from +0.8 to +0.3, because bunker inventory keeps rising with fuel prices and my own caveat on the working-capital release argues against it
'The move is in the guide': the Q4 fuel guide finding moved from -1.2 to -1.5 and abs_move_pct from 6.0 to 6.5 (every HAUTO release carries a new quarterly EBITDA guide); p_up moved from 47 to 46
